## Report

### Actions taken
- Loaded PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md to understand all computational decisions
- Wrote independent Python script (compute_models.py) to recompute both M1 and M2 models from the raw car stopping distance data using f3dasm 2.4.0 ExperimentData
- Executed the computation script which:
  - Loaded data from data/car_stopping_distance (50 samples of x and y)
  - Split into train/test sets (37 train, 13 test) using train_test_split with random_state=1987
  - Fitted M1 model: lstsq of y on [x, x²] (no intercept), computed s from training residuals (ddof=0)
  - Fitted M2 model: lstsq of y/x on [1, x], computed c from residuals of y/x (ddof=0)
  - Computed test set metrics: coverage (fraction within mean ± 1.96 sd) and nll (mean negative log likelihood)
- Wrote comparison script to verify all computed values against expected CSV results
- Generated results/check.md with detailed per-item and overall pass/fail verdicts

### Conclusions
- All 8 parameters for M1 match expected values exactly
- All 8 parameters for M2 match expected values (nll difference is 1e-12, relative difference ~2.2e-13, well below 1e-6 tolerance)
- Both models pass all verification checks
- Data split matches specification: 37 training rows, 13 test rows
- Independent recomputation confirms the original results are correct
